core_obligations: Recall the reduction of the diagonal properties to j (proof lines 2558-2561).
Show j is quasi-compact when U -> S is quasi-separated (proof lines 2562-2565).
Show j is a closed immersion when U -> S is separated (proof lines 2566-2568).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: with the notation and assumptions of the quotient lemma and G finite, if U -> S is quasi-separated then U/G is quasi-separated over S, and if U -> S is separated then so is U/G (source lines 2547-2556). The proof reuses the reduction of the diagonal of the quotient to the morphism j : R -> U x_S U, proves j quasi-compact from quasi-compactness of the finitely many opens g(V) cap V for affines V, and proves j a closed immersion when Delta_{U/S} is one, since R is then a finite coproduct of closed immersions with disjoint images.
